lead: Escondido plumbing deals with hard water, hot inland summers and a mix of older and newer homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Escondido.
risk: hard water scale, slab leaks and aging pipes in Old Escondido
risk_short: hard water, slab leaks and old pipes
why: Old Escondido has homes from the 1900s to the 1940s with galvanized supply lines and clay sewer laterals. Postwar and newer homes across the city sit on slabs.
Inland heat is hard on garage water heaters, and hard water adds scale. California requires water heaters to be strapped for earthquakes.
water: Escondido uses local water from Lake Dixon and Lake Wohlford plus imported water. The water is hard.
tips: Strap your water heater for earthquakes.
Scope old sewer lines before buying.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
areas: PipeMend works in Old Escondido, Downtown, Felicita, Rancho San Pasqual, Kit Carson, Eureka Springs, Mission Park and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Escondido Building Division, and plumbing contractors need a CSLB license with a C-36 classification.

faq.q: Do historic Escondido homes need special plumbing care?
faq.a: Old Escondido homes often have galvanized pipe and clay sewer lines due for replacement. The historic district may have rules for visible exterior work, so check with the city first.
